prompt: Challenge C144-CH2: Downstream purification — specifically the ultrafiltration step — runs at only 55% of nominal throughput because the membranes foul with res

content.text: {"expertise":[{"text":"Polyethersulfone ultrafiltration membranes used in food processing show rapid hydrophobic fouling that degrades performance, and surface modification through zwitterionic polymer grafting can improve flux recovery ratios above 93% after cleaning compared to 51–67% for unmodified membranes.","sources":[{"id":"SYN-PUB-08245","field":"abstract","quote":"Polyethersulfone (PES) ultrafiltration membranes are widely adopted in food and beverage wastewater treatment but suffer from rapid hydrophobic fouling"}]},{"text":"Pre-screening of feed streams through mesh filtration reduces total fouling resistance in polymeric membrane systems, with a 200 µm mesh reducing fouling resistance by 34% in crossflow microfiltration of food processing effluent.","sources":[{"id":"SYN-PUB-08240","field":"abstract","quote":"Pre-screening of the feed stream through a 200 µm mesh reduced total fouling resistance by 34%"}]},{"text":"Tangential flow microfiltration as a pre-treatment step substantially mitigates fouling of microporous membranes by biomass and protein residues in downstream separation processes.","sources":[{"id":"SYN-PUB-08244","field":"abstract","quote":"fouling of the microporous polypropylene membranes by biomass and protein residues was characterised and substantially mitigated by inclusion of a tangential flow microfiltration pre-treatment step"}]}],"fit":"strong","fitReason":"The researcher's publications directly address polyethersulfone membrane fouling in food processing [SYN-PUB-08245], the role of pre-filtration in reducing fouling resistance [SYN-PUB-08240], and microfiltration pre-treatment to mitigate biomass and protein fouling [SYN-PUB-08244], which are the core issues affecting the 36-hour fouling problem in the challenge."}
